I'm researching a specific technical question for the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project (Jira project key SFCC, site zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net, board id 500 "SFCC board"). A team member named Kiera asked a colleague (nickname "Angelo") whether there's a planned "out of the box" (i.e. pre-built third-party library, not custom-built) solution for a calendar/date-picker component shown in a specific Figma screen (file "Zimmermann_Designs", node-id 3193-47937). The screenshot shows: a "Find in Boutique" panel/flyout, with "SIGNED IN AS ANGELA LEE", a "CHOOSE A DATE" section with a full month calendar grid (June 2026, showing all days of the month, one date highlighted/selected), an "AVAILABLE TIMES" section with clickable time slot buttons (9:00AM through 4:00PM), and a "CONTINUE" button at the bottom. The Figma layers panel shows this sits under a "Find in Boutique" grouping alongside other layers like "FIND IN BOUTIQUE modal open" variants.

Important context/discrepancy I've already found in the local repo's requirement docs (.docs/prd/*.md and .docs/integration/*.md):
- "Find in Boutique" is documented as a stock/inventory-check flyout only — it shows per-boutique product availability for a selected product+size via a MuleSoft call, using Google Maps + geolocation (PDP §8, CAI-037–042, PRD-028–039, OM-031). Nothing in its documented spec involves a calendar, date picker, or appointment time slots.
- Booxi (a third-party appointment-scheduling vendor) is the actual system that handles appointments, but the current confirmed PWA scope for Booxi (CRM-165–167, likely Jira epic/stories under an Account or CRM epic) is READ-ONLY appointment history display in My Account only — appointment creation/booking is explicitly documented as "not in current PWA scope... handled in Booxi's own surfaces," with storefront booking scope/timeline still "TBC."
- So a date+time-slot BOOKING calendar doesn't cleanly match either documented feature as currently scoped — it could mean the docs are stale, or this represents a scope expansion (in-storefront Booxi booking now confirmed) not yet written back into the docs, or it's a different/new feature not documented at all yet.
- Also: no calendar or date-picker npm package is installed in package.json at all currently, and there's no existing calendar-related code anywhere in the codebase — so if a decision on an "out of the box" library was made, it hasn't been implemented in code yet, meaning any record would only exist in Jira ticket descriptions/comments (or Confluence, which another agent is checking in parallel).
- One more related data point: the PRD also separately documents a gift-card delivery date picker (GC-005/GC-006) — "calendar with month navigation; restricted to within 3 months from today" — a DIFFERENT feature that also needs a calendar UI. If the team already evaluated/chose a calendar library for that ticket, it might be the same one intended for reuse here.

Please research Jira (project SFCC) and report back on:

1. **Find in Boutique tickets** — search for stories/tasks/spikes with "Find in Boutique" in the summary or description (try JQL like `project = SFCC AND text ~ "Find in Boutique"`). For each, check: does its description/AC/comments mention a calendar, date picker, or appointment time-slot selection? Or do they all match the stock-check-only scope from the docs? Report ticket keys, summaries, statuses, and relevant description/comment excerpts.

2. **Booxi / appointment booking tickets** — search for "Booxi" and "appointment" (e.g. CRM-165, CRM-166, CRM-167 if they exist as Jira keys, plus any others). Check current status and description for whether in-storefront BOOKING (not just history) has since been confirmed in scope, and whether any ticket or comment discusses a calendar/date-picker UI approach or specific library.

3. **Calendar / date-picker component tickets directly** — search broadly: `text ~ "calendar"`, `text ~ "date picker"`, `text ~ "datepicker"`. Also try named libraries: "react-day-picker", "react-datepicker", "react-calendar", "flatpickr", "react-dates". For any hits, report the ticket key, summary, status, and quote the relevant part of the description or any comment that names or discusses a specific implementation approach/library.

4. **Gift card delivery date picker (GC-005/GC-006)** — search for the corresponding Jira ticket(s) (likely under a Gift Cards epic). Check its description, comments, and any linked spike/tech-design ticket for whether a specific calendar library or approach was chosen — this may be the same solution intended for reuse in the Find in Boutique/Booxi screen.

5. **Any ticket referencing this specific Figma node** — search for the Figma URL fragment "3193-47937" or "node-id=3193" or the file name "Zimmermann_Designs" in case a ticket links directly to this screen, which would likely have the most direct answer in its description or comments.

Report back with concrete ticket keys, summaries, statuses, and direct quotes from descriptions/comments — I need to know definitively whether an "out of the box" calendar library was actually decided, and if so which one, or whether this is genuinely still an open/undecided question (say so clearly rather than guessing). This is read-only research — do not modify, comment on, or transition any Jira issues. Keep the report focused and organized under the 5 numbered questions; it will be read by another Claude session synthesizing an answer, not an end user directly.

## Jira Research Report — Calendar/Date-Picker for "Find in Boutique" Figma Screen (node 3193-47937)

**Scope note:** All searches ran against `project = SFCC` on zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net. This was read-only — no issues were modified, commented on, or transitioned. Comment retrieval was validated as working correctly (confirmed comments render fine on SFCC-92, SFCC-241, SFCC-255), so "no comments" reported below for other tickets is a genuine finding, not a tool gap.

---

### 1. Find in Boutique tickets

All hits match the documented **stock-check-only** scope. None mention a calendar, date picker, or appointment time slots.

| Key | Summary | Status | Relevant detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-297** | PDP UI — Find in Boutique Button and Slide-In Panel | In Refinement | "modal/flyout UI showing per-boutique stock availability for the selected size, and all boutique availability states." Real-time OMS call is out of scope (→ SFCC-308). **0 comments.** |
| **SFCC-308** | Inventory – Real-Time Boutique Stock Check for Find in Boutique | To Do | SFCC triggers a real-time inventory call to NewStore OMS via MuleSoft "when a shopper opens the Find in Boutique modal." **0 comments.** |
| **SFCC-458** | Find in Boutique – Buffer Stock Exclusion Logic | To Do | Confirms buffer stock is NOT applied to Find in Boutique — true physical stock only. **0 comments.** |
| SFCC-307 | Inventory (Epic) | To Do | Explicitly lists "Real-time boutique stock availability for Find in Boutique (OMS call via MuleSoft)" and "OMS response caching" in scope — no calendar/booking mentioned anywhere. |
| SFCC-5 | Product Detail Page (Epic) | In Progress | Lists "Find in Boutique modal (per-boutique availability, Google Maps, geolocation)" as in-scope — matches docs exactly. |
| SFCC-9 | Store Locator (Epic) | To Do | Same stock-check framing repeated at epic level. |

**Conclusion:** every Find in Boutique ticket in Jira matches your local `.docs/prd/` scope exactly (stock check, Google Maps, geolocation). Nothing here explains the calendar/time-slot UI in the screenshot.

---

### 2. Booxi / appointment booking tickets

Found **SFCC-72** and **SFCC-626** as the direct Booxi tickets, plus the parent epic **SFCC-16**. None confirm in-storefront booking, and none discuss a calendar/library approach — comments are empty on all three.

| Key | Summary | Status | Quote |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-72** | Booxi Appointment History Integration | To Do | Full description, verbatim: *"Placeholder story - appointment history sourced from Booxi API."* No labels, **0 comments.** |
| **SFCC-626** | My Account – Services Page Layout | To Do | *"Personal Styling tile with 'Book an Appointment' link (routes to Booxi — dependency: SFCC-72)... The Appointments section is built as a placeholder to accommodate the Booxi integration (SFCC-72) without requiring structural redesign when it is ready."* Labels: `CRM-165`, `CRM-167` (confirmed these are requirement-tracking labels, not separate Jira issues — direct lookup of `CRM-165` as an issue key returned "not found"). **0 comments.** |
| SFCC-16 | Customer Account & CRM (Epic) | To Do | *"Appointments section within My Account (Booksy integration — storefront scope and timelines TBC)"* and dependency: *"Booksy — appointment data source for My Account appointments section (scope TBC)."* **0 comments.** |

**Notable discrepancy worth flagging to your team:** SFCC-16 (the epic) spells the vendor **"Booksy"** throughout, while both child stories (SFCC-72, SFCC-626) spell it **"Booxi."** No comment thread anywhere resolves which is the typo. Not directly relevant to the calendar question, but worth a doc-integrity flag since it's the kind of inconsistency AGENTS.md tells you to raise.

Also relevant: **SFCC-525** ("Store Detail – Boutique Services Section", To Do, Squad-B) — the boutique-detail-page version of the same "Book an Appointment" CTA. Its description explicitly says *"the Click and Reserve CTA links to an external reservations flow — the flow itself is out of scope for this epic"* — pattern strongly implies "Book an Appointment" is the same kind of external link-out, not an in-storefront flow. **0 comments.**

**Conclusion:** every Booxi-adjacent ticket confirms the docs' framing — placeholder/link-out/read-only-history only, with scope explicitly marked "TBC" at the epic level. Nothing confirms an in-storefront booking flow has been scoped, and nothing discusses a calendar library.

---

### 3. Calendar / date-picker component tickets (direct search)

- `text ~ "calendar"` and `text ~ "date picker" OR "datepicker"` — **only one hit in the entire project**: **SFCC-386** (see Q4 below).
- Named-library searches — `react-day-picker`, `react-datepicker`, `react-calendar`, `flatpickr`, `react-dates` — **zero hits**, individually or combined, anywhere in Jira text (summary/description/comments).

**Conclusion: no calendar library of any kind has been named in any SFCC Jira ticket.** This is a clean negative result, not an inference — the fuzzy text search would have caught a mention in any field including comments.

---

### 4. Gift card delivery date picker (GC-005/GC-006)

Confirmed ticket: **SFCC-386** — "Gift Card PDP – Delivery Date Picker (Digital Gift Card, 3-Month Restriction)", status **To Do**, labels `GC-005`, `GC-006`, `Custom`, `Squad-A`.

Full description:
> "As a Shopper, I want to select a future delivery date for a digital gift card using a calendar picker, so that I can schedule the gift card to be sent on a specific date. This component appears on the Digital Gift Card PDP only, within the purchase form (SFCC-385). It renders as a calendar date picker allowing the customer to navigate between months and select a future delivery date. Dates beyond 3 months from the current date are greyed out and unavailable for selection (GC-006). Surface: PWA Kit / SFCC PDP page. Owned by: SFCC/PWA Kit. Note: this story is currently created in SFCC-17 (Credit Notes & Gift Cards) for speed but should be moved to SFCC-5 (Product Detail Page)... Depends on GC-005, GC-006. Cross-epic dependency: SFCC-5 (PDP epic), SFCC-385 (Gift Card PDP Purchase Form)."

**0 comments.** No separate spike/tech-design ticket exists for it — `labels in ("GC-005","GC-006")` returns only SFCC-386 itself. Checked the parent purchase-form ticket **SFCC-385** ("Gift Card PDP – Purchase Form...", To Do) too — no additional calendar detail, **0 comments**.

**Conclusion:** this ticket is described purely functionally (month navigation, 3-month cutoff) — **no implementation library is named here either.** So even the one calendar UI Jira does confirm is still an open implementation question, not a decided one. It cannot currently answer "what library was chosen" for the Find in Boutique screen, because no library was chosen for GC-005/006 either.

---

### 5. Ticket referencing the specific Figma node (3193-47937)

- Exact phrase `"3193-47937"` → **zero hits**.
- `"47937"` alone → **zero hits**.
- `"Zimmermann_Designs"` → matched ~50+ unrelated tickets (JQL full-text search appears to tokenize on the underscore and match "Zimmermann" and/or "Designs" as separate stemmed words across nearly the whole project — not a meaningful signal). I grepped that full result set for `calendar|Booxi|appointment|47937` and found **nothing new** — only the same already-covered "Find in Boutique" tickets appeared, incidentally.

**Conclusion: no ticket in Jira links to or references this specific Figma node.** Nobody has filed a story/spike against this exact screen yet.

---

### Bottom line for the synthesizing session

This is a **genuinely open/undecided question, not a documented decision** — say so plainly:

- No Jira ticket documents a date+time-slot booking calendar anywhere in the "Find in Boutique" or Booxi tickets.
- No ticket confirms in-storefront Booxi appointment **booking** is in scope — every reference (SFCC-16, SFCC-72, SFCC-626, SFCC-525) is consistent with your docs: placeholder, external link-out, or explicit "scope TBC."
- **No calendar library — react-day-picker, react-datepicker, react-calendar, flatpickr, react-dates, or any other name — appears anywhere in SFCC Jira**, including in the one ticket that does scope a real calendar UI (SFCC-386, gift card delivery date, GC-005/GC-006), which is also un-implemented and undiscussed (0 comments).
- No ticket references the Figma node 3193-47937 directly.
- Comments are empty across literally every directly relevant ticket (SFCC-297, 308, 458, 72, 626, 16, 525, 386, 385) — this is a project where these particular stories haven't been discussed in Jira's comment threads at all yet, calendar or otherwise. Whatever Kiera and Angelo discussed about an "out of the box" solution, **it has not been written into Jira** as of this check (2026-08-11). It may exist only in Confluence, Slack, or verbally — or it may genuinely still be an open question the two of them were actively working through when that conversation happened.
- One tangential finding worth passing along: the "Kiera" name does appear in Jira, but only in two unrelated threads (SFCC-255 size-selector/"Find My Size" recommendation copy, and SFCC-236 product-card behavior on the Recently Viewed page) — neither is about calendars, Booxi, or Find in Boutique. Don't conflate those with the conversation you're researching.
